dati_metodo: Mixed methods: proprietary data on ventures accepted vs 'almost accepted' to top US accelerators (2011-2012 cohorts, inverse probability of treatment weights), an auxiliary public dataset of VC-raising ventures, and 70 interviews in eight accelerators.

righe.estrazione: The paper finds that some, but not all, of the early accelerators studied aid and accelerate venture development (more funds raised, faster funding milestones), and that learning is a likely key mechanism, with a complementary sorting mechanism. Qualitative fieldwork says participants shifted beliefs about the payoff and risks of planned activities, and that accelerators offer substantial learning benefits early in a venture's life. The txt never frames this as 'resolving uncertainty'; it speaks of learning, consultation and faster funding, and the effect is not universal.
righe.citazione: revealing that accelerators offer substantial learning
righe.frase_paper: Hallen et al. (2020) find that some, but not all, of the early US accelerators they study aid and accelerate venture development, and argue that learning through consultation is a likely key mechanism.
righe.frase_slide: Some, but not all, early accelerators speed up venture development, likely through learning (Hallen et al., 2020)
righe.numero_chiave: 47%-171% more funds raised in the following two to three years by accelerator participants than almost-accepted applicants, in three of four cohorts
righe.limiti_vs_noi: Early US accelerators (cohorts around 2011-2012), small sample of top programs, almost-accepted comparison; not all VC-backed startups and not exit outcomes.
righe.note: Tesi 'resolve uncertainty early' is not stated in the txt: only learning benefits early in a venture's life and belief shifts about payoff and risk (qualitative, descriptive). Shared tesi with yu2020 and gonzalezuribe2018: judged only on Hallen. Effects not universal; authors also find sorting.
